title: Why an open fireplace wastes most of its heat
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why is an open fire inefficient?
Where does the heat from a fireplace go?
Why is a wood stove better than an open fire?

explain.say: Logs store chemical energy, and burning releases it as heat and light. But an open fireplace sends only a small part of that energy into the room.

draw.text: Why an open fireplace wastes most of its heat

explain.say: Most of the room heat comes from radiation: infrared rays from the glowing fire warming whatever is in front of it. That is only about 10 to 20 percent of the wood's energy.
The rest is mostly carried away by convection. Hot gases rise straight up the chimney, and they also pull warm room air with them, so cold draughts come in under doors.
A closed wood stove controls the air and keeps the hot gases inside longer, so its metal body passes far more heat into the room.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Keeping hot gases in means more heat for the room

faq.q: Why do open fires lose so much heat?
faq.a: Most of the heat is in the hot gases, and they rise straight up the chimney by convection. They also drag warm room air up with them.
asks: Where does a fire's heat go?

faq.q: How does an open fire heat a room at all?
faq.a: Mostly by radiation. Infrared rays from the glowing flames and embers warm the people and things in front of the fire.
asks: How does a fireplace warm you?

faq.q: Why is a wood stove better?
faq.a: A stove is closed, so it burns wood with a controlled air supply and holds the hot gases inside longer. Its hot metal body then radiates and convects that heat into the room.
Efficiency is how much of the energy put in comes out as the useful kind. An open fire that gives 15 out of 100 units as room heat is about 15 percent efficient.

faq.q: Why does a room feel cold away from the fire?
faq.a: Infrared rays weaken with distance, and the fire pulls cold draughts across the floor as warm air escapes up the chimney.
asks: Why is it only warm right by the fire?

facts: Open fireplaces typically turn only about 10 to 20 percent of the wood's energy into heat for the room.
Modern closed wood stoves can be around 70 to 80 percent efficient.
